extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty, mathematics teacher educators, and curriculum developers preparing undergraduate courses for pre-service secondary teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, piloting, and evaluating undergraduate curriculum modules that connect college-level mathematics courses to secondary school mathematics to prepare prospective secondary teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessons aligned with specific undergraduate courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessons aligning with courses in single variable calculus, introduction to statistics, discrete mathematics or introduction to proof, and abstract algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The volume provides nine lessons aligning with these courses that include applications to teaching to enhance prospective secondary teachers’ understanding of connections between undergraduate mathematics and school mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend undergraduate mathematics, school mathematics, and teaching without privileging one
rubrics_metrics.description: A robust blend of undergraduate mathematics, school mathematics, and teaching that does not privilege mathematics content over content for teaching or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessons should integrate content and pedagogy so that applications to teaching are treated as equally valuable as other applications (e.g., business or STEM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to mathematics content suitable for inclusion in courses for mathematics majors
rubrics_metrics.description: The lessons attend to mathematics content suitable for inclusion in courses for mathematics majors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material must be appropriate for regular undergraduate math major coursework while also connecting to school mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to mathematics content foundational to teaching secondary mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The lessons attend to mathematics content that is foundational to teaching secondary mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include topics and perspectives that give prospective teachers the mathematical grounding needed for grades 7–12 instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to learning experiences fostered by the teaching materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The lessons attend to learning experiences that are fostered by the teaching materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities and materials that actively foster student learning and deepen understanding, not merely present content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make explicit connections between undergraduate and secondary school mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Making explicit connections between undergraduate mathematics and secondary school mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty should guide students to see vertical connections from school mathematics through advanced undergraduate mathematics, treating these connections as explicit instructional goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop deep, sophisticated understanding of grades 7–12 mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing deep, sophisticated understanding of mathematics taught in grades 7–12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for prospective teachers to acquire a nuanced, advanced perspective on school-level mathematics that informs teaching practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop quality instructional lessons that make explicit connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop quality instructional lessons that make explicit connections between college mathematics and school mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessons should be high-quality curriculum materials that deliberately link undergraduate topics to secondary content and pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot test materials and provide faculty development
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot test these materials and pilot a year-long faculty development program to train faculty on the use of these lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation requires piloting both the curriculum modules and a sustained faculty development program to prepare instructors to use the modules effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research student learning and evaluate faculty development effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Research student learning that results from the use of these lessons, and evaluate the effectiveness of the faculty development program that prepares faculty to use these modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include systematic assessment and research on outcomes to determine whether the lessons and faculty training achieve the intended learning gains and teacher-preparation goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat teaching as a legitimate application of college mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Us Treat Teaching As a Legitimate Application of College Mathematics — explicitly addressing applications to teaching in advanced mathematics courses requires a culture shift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course materials and instructor practice should value applications to school teaching alongside traditional application areas (physics, economics, biology, etc.), embedding teaching-related applications in examples and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial subject-area focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial subject areas for the META Math lessons are: Abstract Algebra, Single Variable Calculus, Discrete Mathematics, Statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project materials should begin by producing modules in these named undergraduate subject areas, ensuring coverage across a range of common courses taken by math majors.
